risk.rationale: Case s.demir@aegean.edu shows suspicious sign-ins from Cloudvault VPS (DE) outside the account baseline (F1, CONFIRMED 0.52, T1078.004) with most sign-ins from DE (F2, LIKELY 0.5), plus a VPN appliance (vpn-edge-01) running firmware with multiple CISA KEV-listed CVEs (F3, CONFIRMED 0.49, T1133/T1190). However, the account takeover is not confirmed as a chain: F1/F2 establish anomalous account usage but do not confirm progression to takeover, and F3 only establishes exposure (vulnerable appliance), not confirmed exploitation. Critically, the data-quality conflict DQ vpn_session_order failing for vpn-edge-01 prevents reliable session ordering/attribution between the VPN appliance and the suspicious sign-ins. Per the decision rules, this is exposure (CISA KEV appliance) with conflicting/insufficient evidence (DQ session-ordering failure), requiring human review rather than automated contain/monitor/benign.
